_comment: Empirical band-widening factors applied at chart render time. Archived round artifacts under forecasts/rounds/ are never modified; the correction exists only in the published fan charts.

source.spec: production_spec: the coverage evaluation re-run with the six Covid dummies (2020Q1-2021Q2) that every published forecast is estimated with, scored on four-quarter differences (coverage_yoy)

derivation: Gaussian half-width approximation: k(h, level) = z(nominal) / z(empirical), where z(p) is the standard-normal quantile at (1+p)/2 and empirical is the measured coverage of the nominal band at horizon h. Each band half-width is multiplied by k around the archived median. k below 1 (an over-covering band) narrows it: this is a calibration, not a one-way widening.
extrapolation: The evaluation covers horizons h1-h8; archived rounds run to 13 quarters. For h > 8 the h8 factor is held constant.
caveat: Coverage is measured on four-quarter differences of the model's log series (pseudo-out-of-sample, overlapping origins), the same year-on-year basis as the published fans. The shock factor is the Cholesky factor (boe-var-model #26/#30), so the measured coverage is the same on every machine. If Bank Rate is ever fanned, use the level factors (band_scale_factors.production_spec), since it is published as a level.
unemployment_satellite: Left raw. The svar-unemployment (Okun) satellite is not among the series in the coverage evaluation, so no measured factor applies to it; borrowing the boe-svar factors would assert a calibration that was never tested. Its fan is labelled as raw model quantiles.
correction: Superseded factors measured without Covid dummies. The coverage run had always estimated with no dummies while every published fan estimates with them, so the factors were derived from a different model than the one they were applied to — and in the same direction at every horizon for UK GDP, which was being narrowed by 36% at h1 where the model actually shown wants 14%. Both sets are published in the source artifact.
standard_error: Binomial standard error sqrt(p(1-p)/n) at the NOMINAL level with n = 50 origins: 0.066 for the 68% band and 0.0424 for the 90% band. Origins overlap, so the number of independent observations is well below n and this understates the true sampling error. A one-standard-error move in measured coverage shifts k by far more than the fourth decimal these factors are quoted to; the digits are the arithmetic of the run, not the precision of the estimate.
